samples.summary: `replaceDocument()` now drops redo, but the interface documents it as a non-write cache sync and `YorkieDocStore` treats it as a no-op — a new store-parity divergence in a method whose whole point is "not an edit"
samples.evidence: store.ts:16-21 documents `replaceDocument` as "Replace the internal document WITHOUT pushing to the undo stack. Used by the editor to sync back after direct Doc mutations that were already preceded by a snapshot() call." `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:863-869` only refreshes `cachedDoc`, so it has zero history effect there; docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:229 says the same ("No-op on YorkieDocStore"). The delta's own stated goal is that the two stores answer the same for history questions, and `willWrite()` here makes them answer differently. Cost is bounded today because no `src` caller uses it (only tests), which is why this is minor rather than major.

samples.summary: The `DocStore` contract in store.ts (the doc callers actually read) was not updated with the two new rules this delta establishes: redo is dropped by a *write*, not by `snapshot()`, and an adopted checkpoint survives an empty batch
samples.evidence: store.ts:48-86 is the canonical cross-store contract (`snapshot()` is described only as "Save current state to the undo stack before a group of mutations", and the batch contract lists "A batch that writes nothing pushes nothing" with no redo clause). The new semantics are recorded only in docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:360-380 and in comments inside `MemDocStore`. A second implementation (or the next store) reading only the interface would not know that clearing redo in `snapshot()` is now a contract violation. No behavioral cost, so minor.

samples.summary: `MemDocStore.batch()` and `MemSlidesStore.batch()` now solve the same seam with materially different undo/redo policies, while store.ts still claims the docs seam "Mirrors `SlidesStore.batch()`"
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1803 pushes a checkpoint unconditionally and clears redo eagerly inside `batch()`, with no adoption, no `wroteNothing` comparison and no per-write redo clear. `MemDocStore.batch()` (memory.ts:222-303) plus `willWrite()` (memory.ts:210) now implements a distinctly richer policy. store.ts:83-84 still asserts the two mirror each other, so the same question ("does an empty batch after a snapshot cost an undo press / keep redo?") gets two answers in the same repo, and the slides in-memory store keeps the behavior this delta argues is wrong. Cost stays inside the codebase (slides has its own contract), hence minor.

samples.summary: Fixing the stranded-trailing-writes case in the store re-introduces, for `MemDocStore` only, the dead Cmd+Z that the adoption logic was justified to prevent: `snapshot(); batch(no-op)` with no follow-up write now leaves a content-identical checkpoint
samples.evidence: The batch now pops only non-adopted checkpoints, so `snapshot(); batch(() => {})` leaves an undo entry equal to the current document (pinned by the new test at test/store/memory.test.ts, 'a batch that writes nothing keeps the checkpoint it adopted'). On `YorkieDocStore` that sequence records nothing, so a slides text box / demo user pressing Cmd+Z after a no-op backspace sees one dead press only in the MemDocStore host. The alternative fit would have been caller-side (`deleteSelection()` not opening a unit it will not write into, or `handleBackspace`/`handleDelete` wrapping the whole action per the todo's "composite actions wrap delete + the writes that follow" item, docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:34). The trade-off is deliberate and documented, so minor, but the divergence it buys should be acknowledged in the design doc's parity claim rather than only the win.

mergedFrom.summary: Every top-level `batch()` now performs a third full-document serialization (`JSON.stringify(top)`) in addition to the existing `cloneDocument` + two `JSON.stringify` passes, on a path that runs once per keystroke in every MemDocStore host. Cheap for a slides text box, less so for the demo app's full document; an identity/generation counter on the checkpoint would give the same answer without the extra O(document) walk.

finding.summary: Adoption fixes only the undo half of the `saveSnapshot(); withUndoUnit(...)` collision; the redo half still diverges between the two stores. `snapshot()` unconditionally does `this.redoStack = []` (memory.ts:183) *before* `batch()` runs, so when the body writes nothing, `batch()`'s `priorRedo` restore (memory.ts:253) puts back an already-emptied stack. On `YorkieDocStore` `snapshot()` is a no-op and an empty batch pushes no change, so `doc.history` keeps its redo entries. The delta's own new documentation asserts parity — text-editor.ts:3831-3836 ("That ordering costs nothing on `YorkieDocStore` ... and nothing on `MemDocStore` either") and docs-collaboration.md:342-353 ("That ordering has to cost nothing on either store"), plus memory.test.ts's existing "a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact" case which encodes the shared contract but does not exercise the snapshot-before-batch shape. Concretely: in a slides text box or the demo app, undo once (redo now available) then perform any editor action that opens a unit and writes nothing (e.g. Backspace at the start of the box, which still calls `saveSnapshot()` above `withUndoUnit`) and redo is silently dead, where the Yorkie-backed docs editor keeps it. The two stores give two answers to the one documented contract.
finding.evidence: memory.ts:177-184 `snapshot() { if (this.batchDepth > 0) return; this.pushUndo(); this.redoStack = []; }`; memory.ts:225/253 `const priorRedo = this.redoStack; ... this.redoStack = priorRedo;`

verdict.reason: The finding's central evidence is not present in the working tree. `MemDocStore.snapshot()` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:214-220) consists solely of `if (this.batchDepth > 0) return; this.pushUndo();` — it does not assign `this.redoStack = []`, contrary to the quoted "memory.ts:177-184". Redo invalidation lives in a private `willWrite()` (memory.ts:210-212) that is invoked at the head of every mutating method (~30 sites, memory.ts:58-471), so redo is dropped by a write, never by a checkpoint. As a direct result, `const priorRedo = this.redoStack` (memory.ts:265) captures a still-populated redo stack when a batch body writes nothing, and the restore at memory.ts:299 puts back live entries rather than an "already-emptied stack" — the redo half is fixed, not divergent. The doc comment at memory.ts:192-208 names this exact `saveSnapshot(); withUndoUnit(...)` collision as the reason for the current design. The finding also asserts no test exercises the snapshot-before-batch shape, but packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts:440-457 ("snapshot() then a batch that writes nothing leaves redo intact") runs precisely that sequence and asserts `canRedo()` stays true and `redo()` restores the text, with the converse guarded at memory.test.ts:459-475. Therefore the claimed store-divergence and the described user symptom (redo silently dead after an empty undo unit) do not exist as described.
